key_insight: A conductive, partly crystalline GaOx hole transport layer can be formed in situ during CuInSe2 co-evaporation, enabling strong back-contact passivation and high-voltage 1.0 eV bottom cells without heavy alkali or Ag additions.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies a practical route to improve tandem-ready CuInSe2 bottom-cell performance by stabilizing the rear interface while preserving a low bandgap absorber and achieving record-level open-circuit voltage.
method: Formed GaOx through ion exchange during co-evaporation of the absorber layer.
Tested whether Cu addition, Na presence, and oxygen-flow conditions affect GaOx conductivity.
Evaluated device performance in CuInSe2 solar cells with the optimized rear passivating contact.
evidence_signal: The optimized devices achieved active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified VOC of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: The conductive behavior appears tied to specific GaOx formation conditions and partial crystallinity, so transferability to other back-contact stacks or deposition recipes may be limited.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
